standard: All requested material parts, independently per answer. Grade the ruling, not support labels.

grades.question: How does each player prepare their ID and Voting cards, what happens to cards for unused colors, and how is the initial Gold Bar pool dealt?
grades.expected_answer: Stand a visible ID in your chosen color, take the matching Voting set, remove target cards for colors not playing, and retain your Ambush card. Put the Gold deck face down and deal four central Gold Bar cards with values hidden.
grades.observed_answer: Each player chooses a color and places that color's Player ID card upright in its plastic stand, visibly in front of them. Give each player the Voting-card set with their color on the backs; remove cards targeting colors not in play and keep their own Ambush card. Put the Gold Bar deck face down beside the play area and deal four cards face down into the center, with values hidden.
grades.reader_evidence: Setup: “upright in their plastic stand”; “Remove cards targeting colors that are not playing”; “Deal four Gold Bar cards face down to the center.”
grades.reason: Explicit upright stand and visible chosen-color ID, matching Voting cards, unused colors removed, own Ambush retained and hidden central4 deal.

grades.question: Is there a player-by-player voting turn order? When may a player change their face-down choice, and when are choices revealed?
grades.expected_answer: There is no turn order. Choices can change until reveal. Once everyone has chosen, all reveal simultaneously.
grades.observed_answer: There is no player-by-player turn order; voting is simultaneous. Each player may change their chosen card until cards are revealed. Once everyone has chosen, all choices are revealed simultaneously.
grades.reader_evidence: Turn Structure: “There is no individual turn order.” Vote: “You may change your chosen card until cards are revealed” and “reveal all choices simultaneously.”
grades.reason: Explicitly states no player turn order, changes until reveal, and simultaneous reveal after all have chosen.

grades.question: In a seven-player vote, Red receives three votes, Blue two and Green two. Is a four-vote majority necessary to make Red a Target? Explain the Target threshold.
grades.expected_answer: No majority is required: the greatest vote total determines the Target. Red alone is Target because three is the highest count.
grades.observed_answer: No four-vote majority is needed. Red is the sole Target because Red received the most votes (three); the Target is whoever receives the most votes, regardless of whether that is a majority of all votes.
grades.reader_evidence: Vote: “The player receiving the most votes is the Target.”
grades.reason: Applies highest count rather than absolute majority: Red alone is Target at three versus two and two.

grades.question: Red and Blue tie for the most votes. With neither playing Ambush, what happens to them, and may someone survive by having voted for either tied Target?
grades.expected_answer: Both tied Targets are eliminated. A non-Target voter who voted for either tied Target satisfies the voting requirement and is not eliminated for voting outside the Target group.
grades.observed_answer: Both Red and Blue are Targets because they are tied for the most votes. With neither protected by a successful Ambush, both are eliminated as Targets. A player may satisfy the voting requirement for survival by voting for either tied Target.
grades.reader_evidence: Vote: “If several players tie for the most votes, all of them are Targets”; “With tied Targets, voting for any one of them satisfies the voting requirement.”
grades.reason: Explicitly identifies both tied Targets, eliminates both absent Ambush, and allows ordinary voters for either to satisfy voting requirement.

grades.question: Blue is the sole Target. Green received no votes and voted for Red. Green did not Ambush. Does receiving no votes keep Green alive?
grades.expected_answer: No. A player who did not vote for a Target is also eliminated, even when nobody voted for that player. Green voted outside the Target group and is eliminated.
grades.observed_answer: No. Green is eliminated: Green did not vote for the sole Target, and receiving no votes does not protect a player. The rule eliminates every other player who did not vote for any Target, subject to the successful-Ambush exception; Green did not Ambush.
grades.reader_evidence: Vote: “Every other player who did not vote for any Target is also eliminated, subject to the successful Ambush exception below.”
grades.reason: Green is eliminated for voting outside the Target group despite receiving no votes.

grades.question: Red plays Ambush, Yellow votes for Red, and Pink votes for Yellow. How are votes tallied, who are the Targets, and who survives after Red's legal retaliation?
grades.expected_answer: Ambush adds no vote. Red and Yellow each have one vote and are tied Targets. Yellow is eliminated; Red survives its successful Ambush and can retaliate only against Yellow, who voted for Red. Pink voted for tied Target Yellow and survives, leaving Red and Pink.
grades.observed_answer: Ambush cards do not count as votes, so the counted votes are Yellow's vote for Red and Pink's vote for Yellow. Red and Yellow tie at one vote each and both are Targets. Red's Ambush succeeds; Red survives and may eliminate Yellow, the player who voted for Red. Yellow is eliminated, and Pink survives because Pink voted for tied Target Yellow. Red and Pink remain for a Final Showdown.
grades.reader_evidence: Ambush example: “Red and Yellow tie at one vote each and are both Targets. Yellow is eliminated; Red survives ... Pink voted for tied Target Yellow and survives.”
grades.reason: Complete vote tally ignoring Ambush, Red/Yellow tied Targets, Red protected/retaliates on Yellow, and Pink survives for voting TargetYellow.

grades.question: A Target successfully plays Ambush and four players voted for them. Do they eliminate all four voters? May they choose a player who voted for another color instead?
grades.expected_answer: The ambusher survives and eliminates exactly one of the players who voted for them. They neither eliminate every voter nor choose someone who did not vote for them.
grades.observed_answer: No. A successful Ambush lets its player choose exactly one player who voted for them to eliminate. They cannot eliminate all four voters and cannot choose someone who voted for another color instead.
grades.reader_evidence: Ambush: “chooses one of the players who voted for them”; “cannot choose an arbitrary player or someone who voted for a different Target.”
grades.reason: Restricts successful Ambush retaliation to exactly one voter who targeted the ambusher; rejects all-voter and arbitrary-color alternatives.

grades.question: A player chooses Ambush but is not among the Targets after the votes are counted. What happens to that player?
grades.expected_answer: The Ambush fails and that player eliminates themselves.
grades.observed_answer: That player eliminates themselves. An Ambush only works if its player is a Target in that vote.
grades.reader_evidence: Ambush: “An Ambush played by someone who is not a Target fails: that player eliminates themselves.”
grades.reason: Non-Target Ambush fails and self-eliminates.

grades.question: Four players survive a vote and its Ambush effects. Does the round award gold now, and who participates next?
grades.expected_answer: The round continues with another conspiracy and vote among the four survivors. It ends when the resolved vote leaves one, two or no survivors.
grades.observed_answer: No gold is awarded yet. With four survivors, the round continues with another conspiracy and vote among the surviving players only.
grades.reader_evidence: Turn Structure table: “Three or more | Continue with another conspiracy and vote among survivors.”
grades.reason: Four survivors continue conspiracy/voting; no gold yet and only survivors vote.

grades.question: Exactly one player survives the round. What reward do they collect, and are the four cards four points?
grades.expected_answer: The sole survivor collects all four central Gold Bar cards. Four bars are four cards, not four points; each Gold Bar is worth 3, 4 or 5 points.
grades.observed_answer: The sole survivor collects all four central Gold Bar cards. They are four cards, not four points: each card is worth 3, 4, or 5 points, so the total points depend on the cards' values.
grades.reader_evidence: Turn Structure: “One | That survivor collects all four central Gold Bars.” Components: “receiving one bar means receiving one card whose value is 3, 4, or 5 points.”
grades.reason: Sole survivor takes all four central cards with3/4/5point values; no unsupported publicity claim.

grades.question: Exactly two players survive the voting. What must they do, which cards does each receive, and how do they choose and reveal?
grades.expected_answer: They must hold a Final Showdown. Each receives Share, Steal and Grab One & Go, may discuss intentions, secretly chooses one card face down, and reveals simultaneously with the other finalist.
grades.observed_answer: The two survivors resolve a Final Showdown for the central Gold Bars. Each takes a set of three cards—Share, Steal, and Grab One & Go—then may discuss intentions and a bargain. Each chooses one card, places it face down, and, when both are ready, they reveal simultaneously.
grades.reader_evidence: Final Showdown: “each takes a set containing Share, Steal, and Grab One & Go”; each “chooses one ... card and places it face down”; reveal “simultaneously.”
grades.reason: Explicit Share/Steal/Grab One & Go set, discussion, secret face-down selection and simultaneous reveal.

grades.question: The final vote eliminates every participant. Who receives gold from the deck, who does not, and what happens to the four central bars for next round?
grades.expected_answer: Nobody receives the central bars. Every player not involved in that final vote receives one Gold Bar from the deck; participants in that final vote receive none. Leave the four central bars and add no new central gold next round.
grades.observed_answer: Each player who was not participating in the final vote receives one Gold Bar card from the deck. Players who participated in that final vote receive no consolation bar for the no-survivor result, including those eliminated in that vote. Leave the four central bars for the next round and add no new bars.
grades.reader_evidence: Turn Structure: “Each player who was not participating in the final vote receives one Gold Bar from the deck. Leave the four central bars for the next round; add no new bars.”
grades.reason: Rewards only those absent from the final vote one deck card each; final voters receive none; all four central cards retained with no additions.

grades.question: Both finalists reveal Share. How many Gold Bar cards does each receive?
grades.expected_answer: Each finalist receives two of the four central Gold Bar cards.
grades.observed_answer: Each finalist receives two Gold Bar cards.
grades.reader_evidence: Final Showdown table, Share/Share: “You get 2; opponent gets 2.”
grades.reason: Share/Share yields two central cards each.

grades.question: One finalist reveals Share and the other Steal. How are the central Gold Bars divided?
grades.expected_answer: The Share player receives no bars and the Steal player receives all four.
grades.observed_answer: The finalist choosing Share gets zero central bars; the finalist choosing Steal gets all four central bars.
grades.reader_evidence: Final Showdown table, Share against Steal: “You get 0; opponent gets 4.”
grades.reason: Steal takes all four, Share takes zero.

grades.question: One finalist reveals Grab One & Go and the other Steal. How are the central Gold Bars divided?
grades.expected_answer: Grab One & Go receives one bar and Steal receives three.
grades.observed_answer: The finalist choosing Grab One & Go gets one central bar, and the finalist choosing Steal gets the other three.
grades.reader_evidence: Final Showdown table: Grab One & Go against Steal gives “You get 1; opponent gets 3”; the note says Grab One & Go always gives its player exactly one bar.
grades.reason: Grab One & Go takes one and Steal three.

grades.question: One finalist reveals Grab One & Go and the other Share. How are the central Gold Bars divided?
grades.expected_answer: Grab One & Go receives one bar and Share receives three.
grades.observed_answer: The finalist choosing Grab One & Go gets one central bar, and the finalist choosing Share gets the other three.
grades.reader_evidence: Final Showdown table: Share against Grab One & Go gives “You get 3; opponent gets 1”; the note says Grab One & Go always gives its player exactly one bar.
grades.reason: Grab One & Go takes one and Share three.

grades.question: Both finalists reveal Grab One & Go. How many bars does each take, how many remain central, and how many new central bars are dealt if play continues?
grades.expected_answer: Each takes one central bar. Leave the other two central and deal just two new central bars for the next round.
grades.observed_answer: Each finalist takes one central bar. Two bars remain in the center. If play continues, add two new bars to bring the central pool to four.
grades.reader_evidence: Final Showdown: “each receives one and the other two bars remain central”; “add just two new bars for the next round.”
grades.reason: Each takes one; two remain and only two new central cards dealt if continuing.

grades.question: Both finalists reveal Steal. What do the finalists and the other players receive, and what happens to the central pot?
grades.expected_answer: Both finalists receive nothing. Each other player receives one Gold Bar from the deck. Leave all four central bars for the next round rather than replacing them.
grades.observed_answer: Neither finalist receives gold. Every player other than the two finalists receives one Gold Bar card from the deck. Leave all four central bars for the next round and add no new gold to the central pool.
grades.reader_evidence: Final Showdown: “neither finalist receives gold”; “give every other player one Gold Bar from the deck”; “Leave all four central bars for the next round.”
grades.reason: Finalists get zero, every other player one deck card; all four central cards retained without additions.

grades.question: When is victory checked, what totals win with 6–9 versus 10–12 players, and who wins if multiple players qualify with different totals?
grades.expected_answer: Check at round end after Gold Bar awards. The threshold is 25 points with 6–9 players and 24 with 10–12. When several qualify, the highest total wins.
grades.observed_answer: Victory is checked at the end of the round, after Gold Bars are awarded. With 6–9 players, the threshold is at least 25 points; with 10–12 players, it is at least 24. If multiple players qualify with different totals, the highest point total wins.
grades.reader_evidence: Scoring: “at the end of a round, after Gold Bars have been awarded”; thresholds are “at least 25” for 6–9 and “at least 24” for 10–12; “the highest point total wins.”
grades.reason: Checks after awards at round end for every outcome; gives 25 for6–9,24 for10–12 and highest qualified total wins.

grades.question: At game end exactly two qualifying players tie for the highest Gold point total. What does the booklet require? If a normal round ends without a winner, which eliminated players return?
grades.expected_answer: The tied players conduct another Final Showdown, repeating until a single player at the table has the highest Gold point total. If no winner ends the game, every player returns next round: stand all IDs upright again.
grades.observed_answer: For exactly two tied qualifying leaders, the tied players conduct another Final Showdown. Showdowns are repeated as necessary until a single player anywhere at the table has the highest gold point total; one extra Showdown does not end the tie if the highest totals remain tied. The summary does not specify how to supply the central pot for these extra game-end Showdowns. If a normal round ends without a winner, everyone returns for the next round, including players eliminated earlier in the round; stand all Player ID cards upright.
grades.reader_evidence: Scoring: tied highest qualifying totals “conduct another Final Showdown” and “Repeat these Showdowns as necessary”; the summary also says the booklet does not “specify how to supply the pot for extra game-end tie Showdowns.” Turn Structure: “If there is no winner, everyone returns: stand all Player ID cards upright.”
grades.reason: Exactly two tied qualified highest players hold further Showdowns until a single highest player exists; all players return with IDs upright if normal play continues.

grades.question: Before each vote, about how long should conspiracy last, may players communicate secretly or by texting/showing cards, and who asks for final decisions when it is time to vote?
grades.expected_answer: Conspire for no longer than roughly a minute and a half. Any overt or covert means is allowed, including texting and showing Voting cards. The game owner asks players for their final decisions before voting.
grades.observed_answer: Before each vote, players conspire for roughly a minute and a half at most. They may communicate by any method, openly or secretly, including texting or showing a Voting card. When it is time to vote, the game owner asks everyone for their final decisions.
grades.reader_evidence: Conspire: “for roughly a minute and a half at most”; any method is allowed, including “texting” and “showing a Voting card”; “the game owner asks everyone for their final decisions.”
grades.reason: Gives approximate90-second maximum before each vote, any overt/covert communication including requested examples, and game-owner final-decision call.

grades.question: When casting an ordinary vote rather than Ambush, which card do you choose and where do you put it? What card replaces that choice if you suspect you are the Target?
grades.expected_answer: Choose the Voting card matching the ID color of the person you want to eliminate and place it face down in front of you. Play your own Ambush card instead of choosing another player’s card if you suspect you are the Target.
grades.observed_answer: For an ordinary vote, choose the Voting card matching the target's visible ID color and place it face down in front of yourself. If you want to defend yourself against being targeted, play your own Ambush card instead.
grades.reader_evidence: Vote: “To target someone, use the card matching that player's visible ID color”; each player places one card “face down in front of themselves”; “To defend yourself ... play your Ambush card instead.”
grades.reason: Target-color Voting card face down in front of oneself, or own Ambush replacement, all explicit.

grades.question: After resolving a vote, how do the Player ID cards show who has been eliminated and who is eligible for the next vote?
grades.expected_answer: Knock over eliminated players’ IDs. Surviving IDs stay standing; only survivors participate in the next vote.
grades.observed_answer: Knock down eliminated players' ID cards. Leave surviving players' IDs upright; they are the players eligible to participate in the next vote of that round.
grades.reader_evidence: Vote: “Knock down eliminated players' ID cards. Leave surviving IDs upright for the next vote.”
grades.reason: Knocks eliminated IDs down and leaves survivors upright/eligible for next vote.

grades.question: A round awards all four central bars, either to a sole survivor or through a Showdown that distributes the entire pot. If nobody wins the game, how is the next central pool prepared?
grades.expected_answer: Deal four new central Gold Bar cards for the next round, keeping their values hidden. Refill to four only if play continues; the retained-pot exceptions apply when bars were left behind.
grades.observed_answer: Because all four central bars were awarded, deal four new Gold Bar cards face down, keeping their values hidden, to prepare the next central pool. If nobody wins the game, this is the new round's four-card pool.
grades.reader_evidence: Turn Structure: “If the entire pot was awarded, deal four new hidden-value bars”; the central pool is dealt face down with values hidden.
grades.reason: Four new central cards face down with hidden values after full award and only if continuing; all requested preparation complete.

grades.question: In the illustrated vote with four votes for Blue and three for Purple, Blue plays a successful Ambush. Does Purple become the Target because Blue survives, and may voters for Purple survive on that basis?
grades.expected_answer: No. Blue remains the Target from the tally, even though Ambush protects Blue. Purple is not promoted to Target; players who did not vote for Blue are eliminated. Blue also chooses one player who voted for Blue to eliminate.
grades.observed_answer: Yes. Blue and Purple are both Targets because four and three are tied for the most votes among those seven counted votes; Blue's successful Ambush does not remove Purple's Target status. Voters for Purple satisfy the voting requirement by voting for a tied Target and may survive, unless otherwise eliminated by a rule such as a successful retaliation. Blue's retaliation is restricted to someone who voted for Blue, so it cannot choose a voter for Purple who did not also vote for Blue.
grades.reader_evidence: Vote: all players tied for most votes “are Targets”; “With tied Targets, voting for any one of them satisfies the voting requirement.” Ambush: it “does not prevent another player from being a tied Target” and retaliation chooses one who voted for the ambusher.
grades.reason: Calls four and three tied vote totals, makes both Blue and Purple Targets, and permits Purplevoters to survive. This contradicts plurality/sourcep7 and the fixed key. Other correct answers and generic self-check do not repair this wrong ruling.

grades.question: Three qualifying players are tied for the highest total at game end. What tie instruction does the booklet give, and does it specify how to arrange a Final Showdown among more than two players?
grades.expected_answer: The tied players must conduct another Final Showdown until a single player at the table has the highest Gold point total. The booklet provides only a two-player Showdown procedure and no arrangement for three or more tied players. A specific multiway procedure is unresolved in this source; do not invent one.
grades.observed_answer: The booklet's stated instruction is that tied highest qualifying totals conduct another Final Showdown and repeat as necessary until one player at the table has the highest total. However, it does not specify how to arrange a Showdown with three or more tied players; the multiway procedure is unsupported by the summary and requires publisher clarification.
grades.reader_evidence: Scoring says tied leaders “conduct another Final Showdown,” but explicitly states: “It provides no arrangement for three or more players tied for the highest qualifying total.”
grades.reason: Question asks whether source supplies multiway procedure: correct full tie instruction plus explicit absence of arrangement. Unsupported procedure/supportpartial label is exactly the disclosed limitation, not a missing requested answer.

grades.question: During an extra Final Showdown between two players tied for the qualifying highest total, both Steal. Could a player outside that pair become the winner if the compensation bar gives that player the single highest total?
grades.expected_answer: Yes. Double Steal gives every player outside the pair one Gold Bar from the deck while the finalists get nothing. The tie instruction continues until any single player at the table has the highest Gold point total, so an outside player who thereby becomes the sole highest wins.
grades.observed_answer: Yes. In an extra Showdown where both tied players Steal, each player outside that pair receives one Gold Bar card from the deck. The outside player's points could make them the single highest-scoring winner; the summary says this can happen.
grades.reader_evidence: Scoring: “The one-bar deck reward for everyone outside a double-Steal pair can therefore make an outside player the single highest-scoring winner.”
grades.reason: All extraShowdown doubleSteal outsiders receive one deckcard and a sole-highest outsider may win; no unresolved requested part.

grades.question: One finalist reveals Grab One & Go and the other Steal. How are the central Gold Bars divided?

grades.observed_answer: The finalist who chose Grab One & Go gets one central bar, and the finalist who chose Steal gets the other three.
grades.reader_evidence: Final Showdown table and rule: Grab One & Go against Steal gives its player 1 and the opponent 3.
grades.reason: Grab One & Go takes one and Steal three.

grades.question: One finalist reveals Grab One & Go and the other Share. How are the central Gold Bars divided?
grades.expected_answer: Grab One & Go receives one bar and Share receives three.
grades.observed_answer: The finalist who chose Grab One & Go gets one central bar, and the finalist who chose Share gets the other three.
grades.reader_evidence: Final Showdown table and rule: Grab One & Go against Share gives its player 1 and the opponent 3.
grades.reason: Grab One & Go takes one and Share three.

grades.question: Both finalists reveal Grab One & Go. How many bars does each take, how many remain central, and how many new central bars are dealt if play continues?
grades.expected_answer: Each takes one central bar. Leave the other two central and deal just two new central bars for the next round.
grades.observed_answer: Each finalist takes one central bar; two bars remain central. If play continues, add two new bars to bring the central pool to four.
grades.reader_evidence: Both Grab One & Go: each receives one; leave two in center and add just two new bars for next round.
grades.reason: Each takes one; two remain and only two new central cards dealt if continuing.

grades.question: Both finalists reveal Steal. What do the finalists and the other players receive, and what happens to the central pot?
grades.expected_answer: Both finalists receive nothing. Each other player receives one Gold Bar from the deck. Leave all four central bars for the next round rather than replacing them.
grades.observed_answer: Neither finalist receives gold. Every other player receives one Gold Bar from the deck. Leave all four central bars for the next round and add no new gold to the central pool.
grades.reader_evidence: Both Steal: neither finalist receives gold; everyone outside the pair gets one deck bar; leave all four central bars and add no new gold.
grades.reason: Finalists get zero, every other player one deck card; all four central cards retained without additions.

grades.question: When is victory checked, what totals win with 6–9 versus 10–12 players, and who wins if multiple players qualify with different totals?
grades.expected_answer: Check at round end after Gold Bar awards. The threshold is 25 points with 6–9 players and 24 with 10–12. When several qualify, the highest total wins.
grades.observed_answer: Check for victory at the end of the round, after Gold Bars have been awarded, regardless of how the round ended. With 6–9 players the threshold is at least 25 points; with 10–12 players it is at least 24 points. If multiple players qualify with different totals, the player with the highest point total wins.
grades.reader_evidence: Scoring: end-of-round check after awards; 25 points with 6–9 players, 24 with 10–12; highest point total wins.
grades.reason: Checks after awards at round end for every outcome; gives 25 for6–9,24 for10–12 and highest qualified total wins.

grades.question: At game end exactly two qualifying players tie for the highest Gold point total. What does the booklet require? If a normal round ends without a winner, which eliminated players return?
grades.expected_answer: The tied players conduct another Final Showdown, repeating until a single player at the table has the highest Gold point total. If no winner ends the game, every player returns next round: stand all IDs upright again.
grades.observed_answer: For exactly two tied qualifying leaders at game end, the tied players conduct another Final Showdown. Repeat Showdowns as necessary until a single player anywhere at the table has the highest gold point total; one extra Showdown does not end the tie if the highest totals remain tied. If a normal round ends without a winner, everyone returns, including players eliminated during that round: stand all Player ID cards upright for the next round.
grades.reader_evidence: Scoring: tied players conduct another Final Showdown and repeat as necessary; if no winner, everyone returns and IDs are stood upright.
grades.reason: Exactly two tied qualified highest players hold further Showdowns until a single highest player exists; all players return with IDs upright if normal play continues.

grades.question: Before each vote, about how long should conspiracy last, may players communicate secretly or by texting/showing cards, and who asks for final decisions when it is time to vote?
grades.expected_answer: Conspire for no longer than roughly a minute and a half. Any overt or covert means is allowed, including texting and showing Voting cards. The game owner asks players for their final decisions before voting.
grades.observed_answer: Before every vote, players conspire for roughly a minute and a half at most. Any communication method is allowed, openly or secretly, including whispering, gestures, showing a Voting card, and texting. When it is time to vote, the game owner asks everyone for their final decisions.
grades.reader_evidence: Conspire: “roughly a minute and a half at most”; any communication method; game owner asks for final decisions.
grades.reason: Gives approximate90-second maximum before each vote, any overt/covert communication including requested examples, and game-owner final-decision call.

grades.question: When casting an ordinary vote rather than Ambush, which card do you choose and where do you put it? What card replaces that choice if you suspect you are the Target?
grades.expected_answer: Choose the Voting card matching the ID color of the person you want to eliminate and place it face down in front of you. Play your own Ambush card instead of choosing another player’s card if you suspect you are the Target.
grades.observed_answer: For an ordinary vote, choose the Voting card matching the color of the player's visible ID whom you want to target, and place it face down in front of yourself. To defend yourself when you suspect you are the target, play your own Ambush card instead.
grades.reader_evidence: Vote: place one Voting card face down in front of yourself; use the card matching target's ID color; use Ambush to defend yourself.
grades.reason: Target-color Voting card face down in front of oneself, or own Ambush replacement, all explicit.

grades.question: After resolving a vote, how do the Player ID cards show who has been eliminated and who is eligible for the next vote?
grades.expected_answer: Knock over eliminated players’ IDs. Surviving IDs stay standing; only survivors participate in the next vote.
grades.observed_answer: Knock down the ID cards of eliminated players. Leave surviving players' IDs upright; those survivors are eligible for the next vote.
grades.reader_evidence: Vote: knock down eliminated players' ID cards and leave surviving IDs upright for the next vote.
grades.reason: Knocks eliminated IDs down and leaves survivors upright/eligible for next vote.

grades.question: A round awards all four central bars, either to a sole survivor or through a Showdown that distributes the entire pot. If nobody wins the game, how is the next central pool prepared?
grades.expected_answer: Deal four new central Gold Bar cards for the next round, keeping their values hidden. Refill to four only if play continues; the retained-pot exceptions apply when bars were left behind.
grades.observed_answer: After checking for a winner, if play continues and the entire pot was awarded, deal four new Gold Bar cards face down, keeping their values hidden. The next central pool is four bars.
grades.reader_evidence: If the entire pot was awarded, deal four new hidden-value bars; new central bars are dealt face down.
grades.reason: Four new central cards face down with hidden values after full award and only if continuing; all requested preparation complete.

grades.question: In the illustrated vote with four votes for Blue and three for Purple, Blue plays a successful Ambush. Does Purple become the Target because Blue survives, and may voters for Purple survive on that basis?
grades.expected_answer: No. Blue remains the Target from the tally, even though Ambush protects Blue. Purple is not promoted to Target; players who did not vote for Blue are eliminated. Blue also chooses one player who voted for Blue to eliminate.
grades.observed_answer: No. Blue remains the Target because Blue has the most counted votes; a successful Ambush protects Blue but does not change which player received the most votes or make Purple a Target. Purple is not a Target on the stated tally of four votes for Blue and three for Purple. Voters for Purple do not survive merely because Blue's Ambush succeeds: they did not vote for a Target, so they are eliminated unless protected by their own successful Ambush.
grades.reader_evidence: Vote: most votes determines Target; every other player who did not vote for any Target is eliminated, subject to Ambush. Ambush: successful protection does not prevent another player from being a tied Target.
grades.reason: Correctly keeps Blue alone Target at4versus3, rejects promoting Purple and eliminates Purplevoters. Generic Ambush caveat is inapplicable to ordinaryvoters, not an actual alternate survival ruling.

grades.question: Three qualifying players are tied for the highest total at game end. What tie instruction does the booklet give, and does it specify how to arrange a Final Showdown among more than two players?
grades.expected_answer: The tied players must conduct another Final Showdown until a single player at the table has the highest Gold point total. The booklet provides only a two-player Showdown procedure and no arrangement for three or more tied players. A specific multiway procedure is unresolved in this source; do not invent one.
grades.observed_answer: The booklet's stated instruction is that tied leaders conduct another Final Showdown and repeat Showdowns as necessary until one player anywhere at the table has the highest total. However, it does not specify how to arrange or conduct a Showdown when more than two players (here, three) are tied; that procedure is unsupported and requires publisher clarification.
grades.reader_evidence: Scoring: repeat Showdowns as necessary; source limitation says card sets, procedure, and payoff table cover only two players and provide no arrangement for three or more tied leaders.
grades.reason: Question asks whether source supplies multiway procedure: correct full tie instruction plus explicit absence of arrangement. Unsupported procedure/supportpartial label is exactly the disclosed limitation, not a missing requested answer.

grades.question: During an extra Final Showdown between two players tied for the qualifying highest total, both Steal. Could a player outside that pair become the winner if the compensation bar gives that player the single highest total?
grades.expected_answer: Yes. Double Steal gives every player outside the pair one Gold Bar from the deck while the finalists get nothing. The tie instruction continues until any single player at the table has the highest Gold point total, so an outside player who thereby becomes the sole highest wins.
grades.observed_answer: Yes. In an extra Showdown where both tied finalists Steal, each receives zero gold and every player outside the pair gets one bar from the deck. The resulting point totals are compared across all players, so an outside player could become the winner if that reward gives them the single highest total.
grades.reader_evidence: Scoring: compare totals of all players after each extra Showdown; outside double-Steal reward can make an outside player the single highest-scoring winner.
grades.reason: All extraShowdown doubleSteal outsiders receive one deckcard and a sole-highest outsider may win; no unresolved requested part.
